# typed-sql 2.4.0

typed-sql 2.4 adds stable build and test integrations through one optional package,
`@typed-sql/build`. Each tool has its own entrypoint, and applications install only the host
tools they use.

## Highlights

- Vite/Vitest, Jest, webpack, Rspack/Rsbuild, esbuild, Rollup/Rolldown, and Next.js share offline
  SQL-file compilation, inline execution plans, source maps, and bounded dependency-aware caches.
- Node SQL-file preloads support the native test runner, Mocha, AVA, and Poku. Bun has build,
  runtime, and test integrations.
- Installation guides cover Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit, and Cloudflare Workers/Wrangler, including a
  real D1 execution example.
- `typed-sql-build types` generates co-located SQL declarations, and `--check` detects stale
  declarations without overwriting application-owned files.
- Jest can delegate TypeScript transforms while preserving mock hoisting, instrumentation,
  source maps, and cache invalidation.
- Existing experimental bridge Vite and Node entrypoints forward to the stable build package.

Eight packed-consumer E2E suites exercise real host builds, test runners, watch invalidation,
production HTTP servers, and Workers/D1. Stable packages remain independent of preview-backed
packages and database drivers.

## Compatibility

The stable package requires Node.js 22.11 or newer. The optional synchronous Node SQL-file
preload requires Node.js 24.11.1 or newer on the Node 24 line, Node.js 25.1 or newer on the
Node 25 line, or a supported later line. Bundler and framework requirements also apply.

Build transforms produce executable JavaScript. Continue using the project checker for inline
SQL inference. Generated SQL-file declarations can be consumed by ordinary TypeScript projects;
the integration tutorials distinguish generated declarations from the project-wide checker.

See the [integration guides](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/integrations/) for installation,
configuration, type checking, and build commands for each target.

## Package tracks

`@typed-sql/build` joins the stable package train. `@typed-sql/ts-bridge`,
`@typed-sql/language-server`, and editor integrations remain experimental. Sharing a release
candidate does not promote their preview contracts.
